newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EIB lending rises to record level in 1996.
newsitem.headline: EIB lending rises to record level in 1996.

text.p: The European Investment Bank, the European Union's main financing arm, posted record results in 1996 with total lending of 23.2 billion Ecus ($27.26 billion), Sir Brian Unwin, president of the EIB, said on Thursday.
To finance the high level of lending, the EIB, the largest among international lending and borrowing agencies, raised 18.6 billion Ecus on world capital markets through bond issues in 22 currencies.
Unwin said the latest results and various activities of the bank underscored its commitment to European integration and a single currency.
"All these activities, by their contribution to European economic integration, will help create the conditions necessary for a successful economic and monetary union," Unwin told a news conference.
Several of the bank's activities in 1996 stood out, he added.

Within weeks of an EU summit in Madrid in December 1995, the bank launched a bond worth 500 million Ecus which included a commitment to convert the total sum into the euro, the single currency, on a one-for-one basis.

More recently, the bank issued a 1.0 billion Ecu seven-year bond which will be denominated in euros when EMU begins in 1999 and a Dutch guilder bond worth 1.0 billion that will be redenominated in the single currency.
For the EU's ongoing energy and transport projects, the EIB lent 6.5 billion Ecus last year.
Outside the 15-nation bloc, total financing amounted to 2.3 billion Ecus, with a record 1.1 billion Ecus advanced to central and eastern Europe.
